mentl/6f66866:
Three probes this tick, all reverted, and two candidates died before a
fix was built on either.

The completion prune is exonerated: bypassing row_keep_completion
entirely leaves the repro accepting, so the param's row var was never in
the frame's accumulated row at exit and the keep-set was never the
question. The charge does run: replacing the call edge's silent
fall-through arm with a visible probe effect produced nothing, so the
bound-TFun arm is taken and inf_add_row_unified fires. row_without_self
is load-bearing: removing it makes the wheel trap outright, which is
evidence the accumulated row contains the frame's own row handle.

The clincher needs no wheel change. A local closure with a concrete row,
declared Pure, refuses with E_PurityViolated, expected Pure but found
effects B. Same call machinery, same declaration; the only difference
from the leaking repro is concrete-row versus free-var.

So the boundary is exact: a declared row is enforced against a concrete
body row and silently vacuous against a body row that is a free var
flowing from a called parameter. The strongest remaining candidate is
that the param's row var unifies with the enclosing fn's own row var,
which it must since the body is f(), and row_without_self then strips it
as a self-reference. The trap probe is consistent with that and does not
prove it, so it stays a candidate.

Next probe determines whether the param's row root equals the frame's
own row handle at exit.

Priority served: the third loop-sized item the standing cursor names --

THE ITERATION KILLED ITS OWN PREMISE. Two iterations ago I banked that
CsUnderscoreRetain is blind: ratcheted at ZERO while `_row` discarded a
proven fact in infer. Reading the detector refutes it. CsUnderscoreRetain
IS drift mode 15 with a precise definition -- a LET whose binder keeps a
leading underscore, an unused value renamed instead of deleted -- and it
correctly reports zero because the wheel has no such let. A
destructure-position `_name` is a different shape, and the accusation was
against a detector for not catching something it never claimed.

THE EXTENSION THAT SUGGESTED ITSELF IS DEAD TOO, and measurement killed it
rather than taste: 293 underscore-named binders sit in destructure position
across src/, 722 underscore-named identifiers overall, and they are
overwhelmingly correct. Naming a skipped field `_spec` or `_h` documents
what is being skipped and reads better than a bare `_`. A shape that fires
293 times on good code is a convention, not a drift, and ratcheting it would
have taught the wheel to write worse patterns.

WHAT THE `_row` BUG ACTUALLY WAS: not "an underscore appeared" but "this
consumer needed that fact and dropped it". Semantic, undecidable by any
name-shape detector, and provably so by those 293. The class belongs to
Hb.audit.carried-truth-projection, which decides it the only way it can be
decided -- by reading whether the GRAPH PROVES a fact the consumer then
failed to use. This is a worked instance of why a text detector cannot
stand in for the audit, which is more useful than the gate I set out to
write.

No gate earned, and writing one would have been the error. Self-build: none;

mentl/6f9363c:
iterate_from(xs, i, n) reads xs[i] = list_index(xs, i) per element. On a
snoc or concat list (tags 1/3, exactly what map/fold/filter BUILD via
push/++), list_index is O(i), so every iteration was O(N^2). perf pinned it
at 48.85% self-time of the self-compile, under the map/fold/filter driver.

iterate now flattens once: iterate_from(list_to_flat(xs), 0, len(xs)).
list_to_flat no-ops on an already-flat list (tag 0), so flat inputs pay
nothing; the flat copy preserves order, so every yield is byte-identical.
The compiler's output is unchanged (m2 == m3 FIXED POINT, not a transition),
only faster: m3-gen 13s -> 10s. list_index dropped 48.85% -> 35.51% self-time
but remains the residual dominant cost (more O(N^2) list_index beyond
iterate_from — the next perf).

8/8 rungs, 66/66 micros, 5/5 crown, m2 == m3 byte-identical (468704 lines).

slot/6f0420e:
Seven valve combinations crossed with the overtone series, drawn as a
7x7 grid in which every cell's intonation error is the row's error plus
the column's. The columns are wrong because a valve adds a fixed length
of pipe cut for the open horn while dropping a semitone requires
multiplying the tube; the rows are wrong because partials are integer
multiples and equal temperament is not. Cents are logarithms, so the
two errors add exactly, with a residual under 1e-12 across the table.

Making that addition visible is the whole object. Switch either layer
off and the rows or the columns collapse to zero. Selecting a cell
decomposes it and plays the note you were aiming at against the note
the tube actually gives you. The mic half reports which partial and
which slot you landed on, always against the real horn regardless of
what the display toggles are set to.

Every number is derived, none measured. tools/horn-check.mjs rebuilds
the horn from first principles without importing anything from the page
and asserts each published figure; tools/checks.mjs drives the live page
over CDP for 51 checks, feeding synthetic tones straight into the pitch
detector because headless Chrome has no microphone. The third-valve
slide throws fall out of the tube lengths at 18.18 mm for low D and
32.91 mm for low C-sharp. Those two are the falsifiable part, and
nothing here has met a real trumpet yet.
